1.title: Text, Speech, Vision and Extraction Capabilities
1.text: Welcome to Module five: Text, Speech, Vision and Extraction Capabilities. It covers the exam area Identify A I concepts and capabilities. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Describe common text analysis techniques, including keyword extraction, entity detection, sentiment analysis, and summarization. Identify features and capabilities of speech recognition and speech synthesis. Identify features and capabilities of computer vision and image-generation models. Identify techniques to extract information from text, images, audio, and videos. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Identify A I concepts and capabilities (forty to forty-five percent). Exam format: a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes; check the exam page for the time. Validated against: the official A I nine oh one study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: Services at a glance
1.text: Services at a glance. Microsoft groups its prebuilt A I services as Foundry Tools (the new name of Azure A I Services). Text analysis. Foundry Tool: Azure Language. Main job: Understand and analyze text. Speech. Foundry Tool: Azure Speech. Main job: Speech to text, text to speech, translation. Images. Foundry Tool: Azure Vision. Main job: Analyze images: captions, tags, objects, text. Information extraction. Foundry Tool: Azure Content Understanding. Main job: Turn documents, images, audio and video into structured output.

1.title: Services at a glance, continued
1.text: Services at a glance. The figure shows this: Four Foundry Tools and what each one does.

1.title: Text analysis techniques (Azure Language)
1.text: Text analysis techniques (Azure Language). Azure Language is a cloud-based service with natural language processing (N L P) features for understanding and analyzing text. Key phrase (keyword) extraction. What it does: Returns the main concepts of unstructured text as a list. Example: "battery life", "screen", "delivery" from a review. Entity detection (named entity recognition). What it does: Finds entities and categorizes them into predefined types: person, place, organization, date, quantity. Example: "Contoso", "Paris", "March three". Sentiment analysis (and opinion mining). What it does: Finds positive, negative, neutral or mixed sentiment, and can link it to specific parts of the text. Example: "The food was bad, but the staff were kind" equals mixed.

1.title: Text analysis techniques (Azure Language), continued
1.text: Text analysis techniques (Azure Language). Summarization. What it does: Extractive: selects key sentences and keeps their original positions. Abstractive: writes new sentences that capture the meaning. Also for conversations. Example: A short summary of a long article. Language detection. What it does: Detects which language the text is in. Example: "French". P I I detection. What it does: Finds personal information (names, numbers) so it can be hidden. Example: Redact a phone number.

1.title: Text analysis techniques (Azure Language), continued
1.text: Text analysis techniques (Azure Language). Microsoft lists P I I detection, language detection, named entity recognition and text analytics for health as core capabilities for new development; key phrase extraction, sentiment analysis and summarization are listed as legacy capabilities (still supported). Exam tip: Match verb to technique: "main topics" to key phrases; "who, where, when" to entities; "positive or negative" to sentiment; "shorten" to summarization; "which language" to language detection. Extractive copies sentences; abstractive writes new ones.

1.title: Speech recognition and speech synthesis (Azure Speech)
1.text: Speech recognition and speech synthesis (Azure Speech). Speech recognition (speech to text). Meaning: Turns spoken audio into text. Features: Real-time transcription (streaming audio), fast transcription (pre-recorded files), batch transcription (large volumes, asynchronous). Speech synthesis (text to speech). Meaning: Turns text into natural-sounding speech. Features: Neural voices (humanlike voices from deep neural networks), custom voice (unique to a brand), S S M L markup to adjust pitch, pronunciation, speaking rate and volume. Speech translation. Meaning: Translates spoken language, speech to speech or speech to text. Features: Live interpretation. Other. Meaning: Language identification, pronunciation assessment. Features: Detect the spoken language; score a learner's pronunciation. Exam tip: S S M L is a markup language for speech synthesis settings. Real-time equals streaming; batch equals many files later; custom voice equals brand-specific.

1.title: Analyze images (Azure Vision, image analysis)
1.text: Analyze images (Azure Vision, image analysis). Caption. A sentence that describes the image; dense captions describe several regions. Tags. A list of recognized things: objects, living things, scenery, actions. Object detection. Which objects and where (bounding boxes). Read (O C R). Printed and handwritten text found in the image. People detection. Where people are, with a confidence score. Smart crop. A crop that keeps the important area. Multimodal embeddings. Vectors for images and text to support semantic search. The Image Analysis four point zero service is deprecated and will be retired on September twenty-five, two thousand twenty-eight. Newer solutions often use multimodal generative models instead (module eleven).

1.title: Image-generation models
1.text: Image-generation models. An image-generation model creates a new image from a text description (a prompt). You can usually choose size and quality. The model name list changes quickly: for example, D A L L-E three was retired on March four, two thousand twenty-six, and G P T-Image models are current. Exam tip: Analyze an existing image equals Azure Vision or a multimodal model. Create a new image equals image-generation model. Where is the object equals object detection. What does the sign say equals Read (O C R).

1.title: Techniques to extract information (Azure Content Understanding)
1.text: Techniques to extract information (Azure Content Understanding). Azure Content Understanding "uses generative A I to process and ingest many types of content, including documents, images, videos and audio" into a user-defined output format. Documents and forms. O C R text, selection marks, barcodes, formulas, layout (paragraphs, sections, tables), and fields you define. Images. A summary and fields. Audio. A transcript, a summary and speaker labels. Video. Key frames, a transcript and chapter segments.

1.title: Techniques to extract information (Azure Content Understanding), continued
1.text: Techniques to extract information (Azure Content Understanding). Ways to get a field value: Extract (the value as it appears), Classify (choose a category), Generate (write a value, such as a summary). Each field can come with a confidence score from zero to one and grounding (the region where it was found). Output is Markdown (for search) or Jason that matches your schema. Exam tip: "Get the invoice total from a P D F" to document extraction. "Get a transcript and speaker labels from a call" to audio analysis. A confidence score tells how reliable a value is.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants the main topics mentioned in thousands of reviews. Which technique fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Key phrase extraction. Key phrase extraction returns the main concepts of text as a list.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A review says "The tent was great, but the zipper broke." The team wants to know how customers feel about each part. Which feature fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Sentiment analysis with opinion mining. Sentiment analysis can be linked to specific elements of the text.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which summarization style writes new sentences that capture the meaning? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Abstractive. Abstractive summarization generates new sentences; extractive selects existing key sentences.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A company must transcribe thousands of recorded calls overnight. Which speech capability fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Batch transcription. Batch transcription processes large volumes of audio asynchronously.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A team wants its voice assistant to speak a brand-specific voice and adjust the speaking rate. What should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Custom neural voice and S S M L. Custom voice gives a brand voice, and S S M L controls pitch, rate, volume and pronunciation.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. An app must find where each bicycle is in a street photo. Which feature fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Object detection. Object detection returns the objects and their bounding boxes.

1.title: Practice Question 7
1.text: Question seven. Which tool turns recorded sales calls into a transcript with speaker labels and a summary? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Azure Content Understanding. Content Understanding analyzes audio into a transcript, summary and speaker labels.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which service analyzes text for key phrases and sentiment? Answer: Azure Language. Question two. What is the difference between extractive and abstractive summarization? Answer: Extractive selects existing key sentences; abstractive writes new sentences. Question three. What does S S M L control? Answer: Pitch, pronunciation, speaking rate and volume of synthesized speech.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which vision feature reads printed and handwritten text in images? Answer: Read (O C R). Question five. What do confidence scores in Content Understanding range between? Answer: zero and one. Question six. What was Azure A I Services renamed to? Answer: Foundry Tools.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Azure Language: key phrases, entities, sentiment and opinion mining, summarization (extractive, abstractive), language detection, P I I. Azure Speech: recognition (real-time, fast, batch), synthesis (neural voices, custom voice, S S M L), translation. Azure Vision: caption, tags, object detection, Read (O C R), people detection; four point zero retires September twenty-five, two thousand twenty-eight. Image generation: creates images from text; model names change. Content Understanding: documents, images, audio, video; extract, classify, generate; confidence zero to one; Markdown or Jason. In the next module, we continue the course.
